business.description: Aptech Limited is a pioneering force in vocational and skill-development training with 40 years of expertise, operating a global network of over 740+ training centers across 240+ cities. The company provides comprehensive learning solutions in high-demand fields including IT Education, Multimedia & Animation, Digital Content & IP Creation, Aviation & Hospitality, Beauty & Wellness, Virtual Production, Hardware & Networking, English Language Training, and Assessments & Training for corporates, educational institutions, and government bodies.

outlook.statement: India's Media & Entertainment sector valued at approximately ₹2.5 trillion, with digital media contributing nearly one-third of industry revenues; AVGC-XR sector expected to require nearly 2 million professionals by 2030; Beauty & Wellness industry expected to create employment opportunities for nearly 3 crore people by 2030; India's Assessment Services market projected to grow from USD 806.68 million in 2024 to over USD 1.2 billion by 2030

Union Budget 2026-27 announced dedicated allocation of ₹250 crore for AVGC-XR sector to build future-ready talent ecosystem; initiatives include institutional capacity building, specialised skilling programmes, AVGC Content Creator Labs, and establishment of Indian Institute of Creative Technologies (IICT) as National Centre of Excellence
Animation and VFX sectors in India projected to grow significantly, reaching Rs 30 billion and Rs 67 billion respectively by 2027 according to EY report 'A Studio called India'
Government's focus on India's Orange Economy on track to generate over 2 million job opportunities in coming years
Institutional Business poised for strategic realignment and long-term growth after 225% turnaround in FY26
Aptech Global Training continues to make lasting impact on global education landscape by bridging skill gaps and empowering learners across continents

The convergence of favourable demographic trends, increasing demand for employability-focused education, government-led skilling initiatives, rapid AI adoption, and the rise of the creator economy present significant opportunities for growth. The company remains focused on expanding its education and skilling ecosystem by leveraging technology, strengthening industry partnerships, introducing future-focused programmes and delivering high-quality learning experiences.

The Institutional Business continues to align itself with national skilling priorities and remains committed to supporting India's human capital development agenda. The company continues to build partnerships and collaborations across the education, skilling and creative sectors.

Recent movie releases indicate that the business for studios is growing. Studios are increasingly integrating AI tools into their existing workflows, and Aptech students continue to be hired by these studios. The demand for AI-enabled talent has also increased.

The 2026 amendment to the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024 imposes a huge responsibility on any entity involved in the public examinations space. The company remains wedded to best processes and upgraded technologies in this space, while weighing the pros and cons of the business opportunity in the light of recent developments.

The Company continued to strengthen its portfolio by introducing industry-relevant programmes in emerging fields such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), Digital Content Creation, Virtual Production, the Creator Economy and advanced manufacturing technologies to address evolving workforce requirements.
India's M&E industry is projected to grow at a CAGR of over 7% between 2025 and 2028, reaching approximately Rs 3,301 billion by 2028.
The Animation, Visual Effects (VFX) and Post-Production industry is expected to witness sustained growth, reaching approximately Rs 138 billion by 2038 at a CAGR of around 10%.

India's test preparation market was valued at USD 11.60 billion in 2025 and is projected to grow at a CAGR of 8.7% between 2026 and 2030, creating an opportunity of USD 6.04 billion during the forecast period.
Indian beauty and personal care market was valued at USD 31.19 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach USD 48.72 billion by 2034, growing at a CAGR of 5.08% during 2026-2034.
Indian IT industry is expected to grow from USD 297.2 billion in FY 2024-25 to USD 315.4 billion in FY 2025-26, registering a YoY growth of 6.1%.

Aptech's business outlook remains positive, supported by increasing demand for quality education, employability-focused training, digital assessments and government-led skilling initiatives. The company expects to benefit from growing opportunities in government and corporate skilling programmes, computer-based examinations and technology-enabled assessment solutions. Continued investments in curriculum innovation including Generative AI, virtual production and creative technologies, along with a strengthened institutional portfolio, are expected to enhance revenue visibility, operational efficiency and long-term value creation.

The Company has been endorsing and practicing best practices towards conservation of environment, people care management and best governance practices with continued efforts over the years. We are fully committed to giving our stakeholders insights into our ESG Journey.

The Company remains committed to responsible environmental practices and continues to explore opportunities to minimise its environmental footprint through initiatives such as optimising energy usage, leveraging digital learning content to reduce natural resource consumption, and promoting sustainable practices across its offices and training centres.

Data Privacy and Cyber Security: Exposure/leakage of sensitive personal data through cybersecurity breaches, digital malicious/hacking activities, student negligence, dedicated cyber-attacks and fraudulent attempts through digital, social media, darknet and other newer technological/Artificial Intelligence threats.

Selling Practices & Services Delivery with Student Tech-Driven Resolution: Unaddressed delivery gaps or misaligned expectations at center level can lead to localized student dissatisfaction, impacting brand reputation and escalating regulatory/compliance risks.

Legal, Compliance and Regulatory Risks: Non-compliance with applicable legal, regulatory, and statutory obligations, as well as governance requirements, may pose significant risks to business continuity. Absence of robust policies and controls to prevent fraud, unethical conduct, integrity breaches, corrupt practices, financial impropriety, and other unfair or unlawful activities may indicate weaknesses in governance framework.

Rapid Technological Change and Industry Skill Requirements: Accelerated adoption of Artificial Intelligence, Generative AI, real-time technologies and other emerging technologies continuously reshaping industry workflows and job roles. Risk of curriculum, faculty capabilities and learner outcomes becoming misaligned with evolving industry expectations.
